Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: Acute onset severely pruritic rash on chest, hands, and flexures; past eczema; no systemic symptoms; minimal response to OTC steroid/antihistamine.

Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript & DDx):  
• Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare – High likelihood: prior history, flexural involvement, dry cracked skin.  
• Allergic/irritant contact dermatitis – Moderate likelihood: acute onset, new distribution, possible unrecognized exposure.  
(Scabies and other causes considered less likely at this stage.)

Working diagnosis: Atopic dermatitis flare.

Management Plan

- Prescribed stronger topical corticosteroid (name/dose/route not documented in transcript).  
- Prescribed emollient bath/shower products; advised regular application for 7–10 days.  
- Prescribed oral antihistamine (Fexofenadine; dose/frequency not documented) for pruritus.  
- Education: keep diary of possible triggers (soaps, detergents, clothing); avoid known irritants; maintain skin hydration.  
- Safety-netting: return in 1 week if no improvement or worsening.  
- No immediate investigations ordered.
